title: Shearing of HMW Bacterial DNA Using MP Biomedicals FastPrep-96 High-throughput Bead Beating System
author: Jae Hee Jang
materials: FastPrep-96 High-throughput Bead Beating Grinder and Lysis System

steps.title: Dilute DNA to target concentration
steps.instruction: In 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes, dilute each sample to contain 1000 ng DNA in a final volume of 50 µL using low‑TE buffer; alternatively dilute directly in a 96‑well deep plate.

steps.title: Load samples into deep‑well plates
steps.instruction: Transfer the diluted samples into two 96‑well deep‑well plates using wide‑bore pipette tips, spacing wells to avoid adjacent or diagonal placement, centering samples, and ensuring plates have equal mass; split samples evenly (e.g., 32 samples → 16 per plate). Two plates are always required (maximum 48 samples per run). If shearing only one sample, fill the corresponding well on the second plate with water to balance.

steps.title: Seal plates with adhesive film
steps.instruction: Cover each deep‑well plate with an adhesive sealing film, making sure the film adheres around the entire circumference of all wells containing samples.

steps.title: Turn on FastPrep‑96
steps.instruction: Switch on the FastPrep‑96 using the power switch located near the lower right corner of the back of the instrument.

steps.title: Set speed and run time
steps.instruction: Using the side dials, set the speed to 1600 rpm and the run time to 22 seconds (00:00:22) for ~18 kb fragments; increase rpm or time for shorter fragments, decrease for longer fragments, but do not go below 1600 rpm for uniform fragment sizes.

steps.title: Insert plates into FastPrep
steps.instruction: Open the clear outer lid, loosen the screw securing the blue inner lid, lift the inner lid, place the two prepared plates (one on each side of the compartment), replace and tighten the inner lid until a click is heard, then close the outer lid.

steps.title: Start bead‑beating run
steps.instruction: Press the green “START” button to run the plates at the set conditions (1600 rpm, 22 seconds) to obtain fragment sizes around 18 kb; adjust rpm/time as needed for different fragment lengths.

steps.title: Spin down plates post‑run
steps.instruction: Remove the plates from the FastPrep‑96 and centrifuge them at 2000 rpm for 30 seconds (00:00:30) to collect liquid at the bottom of the wells.

steps.title: Transfer DNA to PCR tubes
steps.instruction: Using wide‑bore pipette tips, transfer the sheared DNA from each well into 200 µL PCR tubes for subsequent manual cleanup (Post‑Shearing 1× SMRTbell Bead Cleanup, manual version).
